name: RULERv2
description: RULERv2 is a bottom-up benchmark for evaluating long-context language models with a systematic difficulty progression from basic synthetic retrieval to complex reasoning across multiple domains. It isolates specific skills such as retrieval, copying, and problem-solving to better understand model performance degradation with increasing context length.
reputation: A recent long-context benchmark that is gaining attention in the LLM community for diagnosing retrieval and reasoning degradation, but it is not yet as widely established as older long-context suites.
notes: Highlights performance degradation with longer contexts; supports evaluation of retrieve-then-solve and chain-of-thought reasoning strategies.
